notes: Stories refined for clearer separation of contract, core logic, recovery, API exposure, and testing. No new IDs created.

change_log.value: Clarified schema includes retry policy, error taxonomy, fallback semantics, and response envelope aligned to existing pipeline patterns
Explicitly includes temp-file strategy, atomic rename, checksum validation, and last-known-good recovery pointer
Scoped to internal APIs and debug surfaces only; no external/public exposure
Expanded to include fault injection (disk full, permission errors, file locks) and deterministic replay scenarios

stories.title: File Operation Resilience Contract and Error Schema
stories.description: Define a standard contract for local file operations including retry policy, error classification (transient vs fatal), fallback behavior, and a unified response schema aligned with existing pipeline and logging patterns.

stories.title: Retry and Backoff Engine for File Operations
stories.description: Implement core retry logic with exponential backoff, jitter, and max retry thresholds for local disk operations, handling transient I/O errors such as file locks and partial availability.

stories.title: Fallback and Atomic Write Recovery Mechanism
stories.description: Implement safe file write patterns including temp-file writes, atomic renames, checksum validation, and rollback to last-known-good state to prevent propagation of corrupted or partial files.
stories.evidence: ASSUMPTION: No atomic write or rollback safeguards exist; GAP requires temp-file + rename pattern and recovery handling

stories.title: Expose File Resilience Status via Internal APIs
stories.description: Expose resilience outcomes (retry count, fallback usage, error classification) through internal service interfaces and debug logging surfaces for pipelines and ops tooling.

stories.title: File Operation Resilience Test Suite
stories.description: Develop unit and integration tests with fault injection (disk full, permission errors, file locks, interrupted writes) to validate retry behavior, atomicity, and recovery integrity across services.
